sentence: Bravo Six Actual, this is Charlie Two-One. SITREP follows. Currently OP at grid four-seven-bravo, holding the high ground vicinity of OBJ Falcon. Two enemy squad-sized elements observed moving west at six hundred meters, BMNT plus fifteen. We are amber on ammo, green on water, yellow on comms. No friendly casualties. Request guidance on engagement criteria and possible CAS on station. Charlie Two-One, over.

All stations, this net, SITREP at zero-six-hundred local. BLUEFOR has consolidated on Phase Line Tango. REDFOR appears to be repositioning to the north, likely a forward passage of lines. Combat power assessed at eighty-five percent. CL III and CL V resupply expected by LOGPAC at twelve hundred. Continue current task and purpose until further FRAGO. How copy, over.

Higher, this is Tango Three-Six. Negative contact past four hours. Patrol cleared the named area of interest, ENY ACTY remains low. Local nationals cooperative, atmospherics permissive. Will RTB at one-four-three-zero. Recommend follow-on element relieve in place NLT one-five-hundred. Will pass detailed debrief upon return to FOB. Three-Six, over.

Standby for SITREP, break. Element strength is one-six pax, all accounted for. We are FOLO on the assault objective. Demolition team has placed charges on the bunker complex, timed for plus ten. Sniper team in overwatch reports clear sectors of fire. Awaiting your execute on the demo, then we collapse back to the assembly area. Acknowledge, over.

TOC, Patrol Six. Spot report. One vehicle, technical-type, mounted heavy machine gun, observed at MSR Tampa, grid Mike-Romeo eight-eight-two-three-four-five. Vehicle is stationary, two PAX dismounted, posture unknown. Requesting permission to engage with organic assets or vector air. Stand by for further. Patrol Six, out.

Operations, this is the company commander. Personnel status: ninety-six out of one hundred and twelve, four on quarters. Equipment readiness: vehicles green, comms green, NVGs amber pending fresh batteries on the LOGPAC. Training: company conducted live fire reflexive engagement, all squads passed. No Class A incidents this reporting period. Will brief BC at the eighteen hundred huddle. Over.

Roger your last, transmitting SITREP. Forward observer reports adjusting fires on TRP Two-Four. First round splash in three-zero seconds. Maneuver element in support by fire is set. Breach element is at the release point. We are five mikes to assault initiation. Recommend you confirm CAS holding at the IP. Acknowledge receipt. How copy, over.

All BLUEFOR elements, hourly SITREP. North sector quiet, no movement reported. East sector reports two suspicious dismounts vicinity Checkpoint Seven, currently being shadowed by Scout One. South sector all secure, OP rotations on schedule. West sector reports HMMWV deadlined for maintenance, recovery vehicle dispatched. Battalion staff duty notified. Continue normal posture. Out.

Zero-Five, this is Two-Six. Negative SIGACTS past twelve hours. Patrol coverage is continuous across AOR. ANSF partner force is integrated into rotation, performing at acceptable standard. Local elder shura completed without incident, key leader engagement notes will follow by chat. Combat power remains green across all WARNORDs in effect. Two-Six, out.

Battle Captain, end-of-mission SITREP. Objective Hawk cleared and secured. EPW count is four, processed and evacuated to the holding area. Sensitive site exploitation conducted, three laptops and two cell phones in the SSE bag. No friendly KIA, two WIA, Cat C, both evac to Role Two. Recommend extending the cordon for an additional six hours pending EOD sweep. Standing by for guidance, over.

Steel Six-Four, this is Observer Two-One. Fire mission, polar. Direction two-eight-four-zero mils, distance one-two-hundred, dropping fifty. Target description: enemy squad in the open, danger close. Request high explosive in effect, point detonating. Three rounds, fire for effect. Method of fire and control, at my command. Over.

Adjust fire, target Alpha Bravo two-two-four-five. Grid mike-tango niner-eight-four-three-two-one. Target description: dismounted infantry occupying treeline, estimated platoon strength. Marking round, white phosphorus. Will adjust. Request immediate suppression for two minutes, then shift to creeping barrage one hundred meters north. Confirm guns ready to fire. Over.

Splash, out. Spotting round was over and right, one hundred meters and fifty meters respectively. Left one-zero-zero, drop five-zero, fire for effect. Three rounds, HE quick. Maneuver element is set and ready to assault on cessation of fires. Mark final protective fires on TRP Three, hold those for the FPF call. Acknowledge, over.

Battery, fire mission, area target. Center of mass grid romeo-papa three-four-five-six-seven-eight. Length four hundred, width two hundred, attitude one-six-zero-zero mils. Enemy mortar position, low priority danger close to friendly element on western flank. Method, two volleys, time on target one-four-three-zero. ICM in effect, then DPICM follow-on. Stand by, fire for effect on my command.

Right two-zero, add five-zero, repeat. Effects on target observed, enemy element neutralized, estimated seventy percent casualties to the target. Cease fire, cease fire. End of mission. Surveillance, two enemy KIA, multiple WIA observed displacing east toward the wood line. Request shift to TRP Seven for follow-on suppression as they move. Over.

Guns up, ready to fire. Charge four, white bag. Fuze quick. Deflection three-two-four-eight, quadrant three-six-five. Time of flight three-six seconds. Shot, out. Splash in zero-five. Forward observer, this is Fire Direction Center, all rounds complete, awaiting your battle damage assessment. Stand by for next mission. Out.

Mortar section, fire mission, grid mission. Target description: enemy mortar baseplate suspected vicinity grid hotel-juliet four-five-six-seven-eight-niner. Two tubes, four rounds high explosive each. At my command. Smoke screen to follow on order, two rounds, two-hundred meters west of target, to cover maneuver element withdrawal back to the rally point. Confirm.

Forward observer to FDC, request final protective fires on FPF Echo. Direction one-six-zero-zero mils. Enemy attempting to breach our wire. Continuous illumination on TRP One, sustained until further orders. We are pinned in our primary fighting positions. Confirm FPF rounds outbound. Acknowledge time of flight. Over, urgent.

Steel Rain, this is Eagle Eye. Suppress, suppress, suppress. Grid Mike-Lima eight-seven-six-five-four-three, troops in contact, danger close. Friendly element in defilade behind ridge to the south. Initials only, three rounds high explosive, then I will assess. Confirm gun-target line clear of friendly elements. Stand by, over.

Section, fire mission. Polar mission from OP Two. Direction four-five-zero-zero mils, distance eight-five-zero meters, drop one-zero-zero. Hostile sniper position in second story of structure designated Building Seven. Request precision-guided munition if available, otherwise standard HE with delay fuze for penetration. Time on target as soon as practical. Maneuver in support by fire awaiting splash.

Authentication challenge, Alpha-Tango. Authentication response should be Foxtrot-Niner. Negative response, this station unable to authenticate. Suspect compromised callsign. Switch to alternate frequency Charlie at this time. All stations roger up by callsign in order: Tango-Six, Romeo-Three, Whiskey-Two. Out.

I spell the grid for you. Hotel, India, Delta, Echo, break. Then numerics six, eight, four, two, five, niner. Read back. Negative, my last, second letter is India not Indigo, third is Delta not Dakota. Use standard phonetic only. Confirm correct grid before plotting. Over.

Code word for tonight is Sierra-Mike-Oscar-Kilo-Echo, response Foxtrot-India-Romeo-Echo. Use proword 'Authenticate' only when challenging unknown callsigns. If response is incorrect or delayed beyond five seconds, assume the station is compromised and refer immediately to the duty signal officer. Codewords rotate at zero-zero-zero-one Zulu.

Convoy designation is Lima-Papa Two-Seven, all stations acknowledge by element. Lead vehicle is Lima-Papa Two-Seven Alpha. Trail vehicle is Lima-Papa Two-Seven Bravo. Casualty collection point in the convoy is the third vehicle, designated Charlie. Communications check at start point, ten minutes prior to roll. Use phonetic letters only on the net, no abbreviations.

Roger Tango-Six. My grid is Mike-Romeo six-four-niner-three-two-one. I spell, Mike-Mike, then Romeo as in Romeo. Numbers as said. Vehicle bumper number is Hotel-Quebec-One-One-Zero. Read back time now and location. All transmissions in clear, this net is unsecure pending crypto fill at zero-eight-hundred. Acknowledge, over.

Designate the objective as Objective Whiskey-Charlie. Primary breach point is Breach Point Tango. Secondary is Breach Point Uniform. Support by fire position is Sierra-Bravo-Foxtrot. Rally point one is Romeo-Papa One, rally point two is Romeo-Papa Two. All elements memorize and confirm before stepping off. Out.

All callsigns prefixed by Alpha for first platoon, Bravo for second, Charlie for third, Hotel for headquarters. Platoon sergeants append Seven, platoon leaders Six. So Bravo Six is second platoon leader, Charlie Seven is third platoon sergeant. Higher is Mike Six. Confirm understanding by callsign on this net, in sequence. Over.

Code word for emergency extraction is Sierra-Echo-Echo, repeated three times. Code word for medical emergency is Niner-Lima, repeated. Code word for compromise of position is Bravo-Bravo. Use only when conditions warrant. Misuse will be debriefed. Maintain phonetic discipline on all nets. Out.

Friendly aircraft on station, callsign Hawg One-Two, type Alpha-One-Zero. Frequency Uniform-Hotel-Foxtrot pre-set channel four. IFF squawking Mode Three correct. Visual identification, single ship, low and west. Friendly mark with VS-17 panel orange side up, supplemented by Sierra-Bravo for night identification. Acknowledge.

Communications check, this net, this frequency, Lima-Charlie, how copy. Lima-Charlie back, read you five by five. Pass to all stations: switch to alternate Charlie at one-six-three-zero local. Authentication code rolls at one-eight-hundred. Pro-words this period are 'Authenticate' and 'Verify'. Use phonetic for all callsigns and grids. Out.

Break, break, MEDEVAC, MEDEVAC, MEDEVAC. Line One, grid mike-tango eight-eight-three-four-six-two. Line Two, frequency four-three-decimal-five-five, callsign Doc Seven. Line Three, one urgent surgical, two priority. Line Four, no special equipment required. Line Five, three litter, no ambulatory. Line Six, no enemy in area, LZ secure. Line Seven, mark with VS-17 panel. Line Eight, US military. Line Nine, light vegetation, suitable for UH-60. How copy, over.

Doc Six, this is Hotel Two-Three Echo. Requesting MEDEVAC. Nine-line follows. Pickup site is grid romeo-bravo two-seven-five-three-eight-one. Three patients, one Cat A gunshot wound to chest, sucking chest wound treated with occlusive dressing. Two Cat B fragmentation wounds, ambulatory. LZ is secure, marked with red smoke at time of arrival. Send aircraft on direct, ETA priority for the Cat A. Over.

MEDEVAC request, urgent. Line One: grid four-five-six-seven-eight-niner. Line Two: this freq, callsign Two-Six. Line Three: A is urgent, one patient, blast injury, both lower extremities, tourniquets in place. Line Four: none. Line Five: one litter. Line Six: Charlie, possible IDF in vicinity, recommend gunship escort. Line Seven: smoke on arrival, color last. Line Eight: alpha, US military. Line Nine: rocky, suitable hoist only.

Standby for MEDEVAC nine-line, breaking down by line. Line One grid will be passed in clear with phonetic letters. Line Two callsign and frequency for the requesting unit. Line Three patient precedence A urgent, B urgent surgical, C priority, D routine, E convenience. Line Four equipment, A none, B hoist, C extraction, D ventilator. Continue through line nine before transmitting.

Bird inbound, three mikes out. Mark LZ with VS-17 panel, orange side up. Wind from the south at five knots, indicate by smoke as the aircraft approaches. Casualty packaged on litter, IV established, fluid running TKO. Tourniquet times annotated on the forehead. Casualty card complete and stapled to the patient. Stand by for hoist ops.

Nine-line, nine-line, nine-line. Pickup is at grid alpha-bravo seven-seven-two-niner-zero-one. Two patients, both Cat A, one penetrating abdominal trauma, one severe head injury, both unresponsive. Hoist required, dense canopy on the X. Hostile contact possible within the last hour, recommend escort. Mark with chem light buzzsaw at night. Send. Over.

Receiving facility is Role Two Whiskey-Tango. Aircraft is Dustoff Two-Five, callsign Dustoff Two-Five. Inbound to LZ Mike, ETA four mikes. Confirm patient packaged, sensitive items consolidated, weapons cleared and tagged. Notify gaining medical officer of MIST report en route on freq Bravo. Out.

Negative on hoist, ground evac required. Vehicle is M997 ambulance, callsign Doc Three. Route from current location to Role One is one-six clicks via MSR Boston. Escort is one MRAP, callsign Gunship Two. Departure ten mikes. Patient is one priority, gunshot wound to thigh, bleeding controlled, hemodynamically stable. Update upon arrival.

Line three precedence breakdown: Alpha is life threatening within two hours, Bravo urgent surgical needs immediate surgery, Charlie priority within four hours, Delta routine within twenty-four hours. We are calling Alpha on this patient due to airway compromise and falling sat. Confirm bird is closest available with onboard medical attendant.

End of mission, MEDEVAC complete. Patient handed over to flight medic at one-three-four-five local. Casualty card and TCCC card transferred with the patient. LZ closed, panel and smoke recovered. Element collapsing back to assembly area. Higher notified of patient destination and condition. Out.

Paragraph one, situation. Enemy forces consist of a reinforced motorized rifle platoon believed to be defending the objective with prepared fighting positions and possible obstacle belt to the east. Friendly forces, our higher is conducting a battalion-level attack to seize OBJ Tiger by zero-six-hundred. Attachments and detachments are one engineer squad attached, no detachments. Civil considerations: minimal local population in the AO.

Paragraph two, mission. First platoon attacks NLT zero-three-zero-zero local on six May to seize OBJ Falcon in order to enable second platoon's follow-on attack on OBJ Hawk. Paragraph three, execution. Commander's intent, key tasks, end state. Concept of the operation: support by fire, breach, assault. Tasks to subordinate units, coordinating instructions, including PIRs and CCIRs.

Paragraph four, sustainment. Logistics: Class I, three days MRE on the man, water resupply by LOGPAC at phase line Bravo. Class III not required for this dismounted operation. Class V, basic load plus one bandolier per rifleman, double basic on grenades. Class VIII, combat lifesaver bag at squad level, aid station co-located with company TOC.

Paragraph five, command and signal. Command, succession of command is platoon leader, platoon sergeant, first squad leader. Higher commander is at company TOC, callsign Mike Six. Signal, primary is FM secure freq Alpha, alternate is FM secure freq Bravo, contingency is line of sight, emergency is signal mirror or smoke. Code words and challenge-pass per signal annex.

Commander's intent: deny the enemy use of the high ground vicinity OBJ Eagle through a hasty defense, while preserving combat power for follow-on offensive operations. Key tasks: occupy primary battle positions, emplace obstacles, integrate indirect fires into the engagement area. End state: friendly element holds OBJ Eagle, enemy combat power reduced by fifty percent, ready to transition to attack on order.

Concept of operation: this is a deliberate attack with three phases. Phase one is movement to the assault position, executed under cover of darkness using infiltration. Phase two is the assault, initiated by SBF lifting fires from TRP Two to TRP Five, breach element follows with the assault element close behind. Phase three is consolidation and reorganization on the objective.

Tasks to subordinate units. First squad: support by fire from SBF position one, suppress enemy positions on OBJ Tango from H-hour minus five to H-hour plus ten. Second squad: breach the wire obstacle at the designated breach point, establish near and far side security. Third squad: assault through the breach, clear trenches from west to east. Weapons squad: provide overwatch from SBF position two.

Coordinating instructions include time of attack, no later than zero-four-three-zero. ROE in effect is positive identification required before engagement. PIRs: enemy command and control nodes, enemy reinforcement routes, civilian movement on the objective. Risk assessment: moderate, mitigated by rehearsals, pre-combat checks, pre-combat inspections, and detailed terrain study using the sand table.

Service and support: maintenance teams are positioned at the assembly area with one wrecker on standby for vehicle recovery. Casualty evacuation flows through the company CCP, then to Role One at the battalion aid station. EPW handling per the FRAGO annex, search, silence, segregate, safeguard, speed, tag. All sensitive items inventoried before crossing the line of departure.

Are there any questions on this order? Time check, my time is zero-two-three-five local in three, two, one, hack. Next time hack at zero-three-hundred. Brief-back from squad leaders required NLT zero-two-five-zero. Rehearsals: full mission rehearsal at zero-three-one-zero, actions on the objective rehearsal at zero-three-three-zero. Out.

Maintain strict net discipline. Unauthorized chatter, location pinpointing in clear, and personal names are prohibited on all tactical nets. Use only assigned callsigns. Transmissions should be brief, accurate, and clear. Pro-words only, no slang. Hot mike will be jumped on immediately. Any station hearing dead air or unidentified transmissions report to the net control station.

Charlie Six, this is Alpha Six Actual. Be advised, dropping off this net for the next two-zero mikes. Alpha Six Mike will assume the radio. Callsign authority is delegated for routine traffic only. For any TIC or critical updates, push to alternate freq Bravo and they will reach me by relay. Acknowledge.

All callsigns Echo on this push, conduct radio check by tac-org. Echo Six, Echo One-Six, Echo Two-Six, Echo Three-Six, Echo Four-Six in sequence. Standby. If you do not hear me when I call you, report immediately to NCS on backup frequency. Crypto roll is at one-eight-hundred, fills on hand at each station before sundown.

Net Control Station, this is Tango Three-Six. Request permission to break squelch for traffic. Wait, out. Tango Three-Six, this is NCS, you are clear to send. Send your traffic. Roger, sending in two parts. Part one, situation report. Part two, request for resupply. Stand by, part one to follow.

Stations using callsign 'Actual' should be the principal, not the radio operator. If the principal is unavailable, use the callsign without 'Actual'. Do not impersonate Actual unless explicitly delegated. Authentication required when 'Actual' is unexpectedly on the net. Confirm by codeword Romeo-Sierra before passing sensitive traffic. Out.

Negative, this is Hotel Two-Three, you are unreadable. Say again all after 'phase line'. Hotel Two-Three, this is Hotel Six, I say again, all after phase line, phase line Tango. Tango as in Tango. Do you copy now. Roger, good copy, switching to alternate frequency for clarity. Out.

Callsign assignments for this exercise: Bravo Company is Bear, Charlie Company is Crow, Headquarters is Hammer. Platoons append numerics: Bear One, Bear Two, Bear Three. Specialty platoons: mortars are Steel, scouts are Sabre, medics are Doc. All callsigns published in signal annex Charlie. Memorize and confirm. Out.

Whiskey Six Actual, this is Whiskey Three-Six. Spot report, two enemy on foot, vicinity of grid juliet-kilo seven-six-four-eight-niner-zero. Posture is moving south at walking pace. No weapons visible. Recommend continued observation, requesting no engagement at this time. Will continue to track and report. Three-Six, out.

All stations on this net, jump frequencies in two mikes. Primary becomes Charlie, alternate becomes Delta. Confirm crypto fills loaded for both. If unable to load fills, report to NCS on backup analog. Time hack to follow: my time is one-three-three-three local in three, two, one, mark. Out.

Roger that, Lima Two-Six. Wait, out. Coming back to you. Negative on your last request, higher denies movement to phase line Bravo at this time. Hold at phase line Alpha until further. Reason follows: enemy ACTY observed in NAI Six, deconfliction required with the aviation element. Stand by for FRAGO. Out.

BLUEFOR maneuver brigade is conducting a deliberate attack against REDFOR mechanized regiment occupying defensive positions in sector. OPFOR has emplaced obstacle belts forward of phase line Tango and a counterattack force in depth at engagement area Spear. BLUEFOR scheme of maneuver is a single envelopment from the south, with a supporting attack to fix REDFOR in the north. Brigade reserve will be committed on order to exploit the breach.

REDFOR commander has decided to conduct a hasty defense in sector. Forward security element will conduct delay forward of phase line Alpha. Main defensive belt anchored on the high ground vicinity OBJ Wolf. Counterattack force of one mechanized company in depth. EA development includes overlapping fires from key weapon systems, obstacle integration with direct and indirect fires.

OC/T notes from the rotation: BLUEFOR struggled with synchronization of fires and maneuver at the breach. REDFOR exploited the gap between phase line Alpha and Bravo by infiltrating a recon element through unobserved terrain. Recommend increased emphasis on the IPB process, particularly modified combined obstacle overlay analysis, prior to next iteration of the exercise.

MILES casualty cards collected from the lane reflect a BLUEFOR to REDFOR loss ratio of three to one, unfavorable for the attacker. After action review will focus on actions on the objective, particularly consolidation and reorganization, where BLUEFOR was caught by REDFOR's local counterattack while still in the disorganized phase. Lessons learned to be integrated into the next training cycle.

REDFOR has demonstrated proficiency in operating inside BLUEFOR's decision cycle by using deception, decoy positions, and aggressive counter-recon. BLUEFOR S-2 assessed REDFOR battle position incorrectly during the IPB phase, leading to a misdirected supporting attack. Recommend integration of red-teaming into the planning process going forward.

Exercise control has called administrative freeze for one-five mikes to reposition observer-controllers. BLUEFOR and REDFOR commanders will remain in current locations. No movement on either side, no fires, no comms traffic except admin. Resumption signal will be three flares, green, on the master grid. Use this time to consolidate logs and prepare for AAR. Out.

BLUEFOR aviation task force conducted a deep attack on REDFOR artillery positions vicinity NAI Seven. Battle damage assessment from the OC/T cell awarded six destroyed howitzers and two destroyed command vehicles. REDFOR fires capability significantly degraded for the next twenty-four hours of the exercise. BLUEFOR ground commander has windowed initiation of the main attack as a result.

Force-on-force engagement at the urban training complex requires strict adherence to safety protocols. All weapons cleared and inspected, MILES gear functional, eye and ear protection, no live ammunition or pyrotechnics inside the structures. BLUEFOR and REDFOR will employ realistic small unit tactics, but training scars from prior rotations must not bleed into doctrinal application. OC/Ts will adjudicate disputed engagements.

REDFOR doctrinal template assesses a motorized rifle company in the defense holding a frontage of approximately fifteen hundred meters with two platoons forward and one in depth. Crew-served weapons emplaced to provide interlocking sectors of fire, anti-tank weapons sited along likely armor avenues of approach, sappers prepared to execute reserve demolitions on key terrain. BLUEFOR must respect this template in scheme of maneuver development.

End of training day, BLUEFOR brigade is at REDCON-3, REDFOR motorized regiment at REDCON-2 pending overnight reset. Both sides will conduct standdown actions, weapons cleared, vehicles into the maintenance posture, leadership huddle for the daily AAR at the BDOC. Exercise will resume at zero-six-hundred local with the FRAGO already disseminated. OC/T cell will be on call overnight.

Force protection posture is currently FPCON Bravo. All entry control points are double manned, vehicle searches randomized at twenty-five percent of inbound traffic, secondary inspection mandatory for any vehicle without proper credentials. Standoff distance from perimeter berms is maintained at one hundred meters minimum. Quick reaction force is on five-minute alert status. Sleeping quarters are dispersed in accordance with the threat assessment.

Threat update has elevated FPCON to Charlie based on credible reporting. All personnel are confined to garrison. Off-post travel is suspended pending further notice. ECP procedures are heightened, all vehicles searched on entry, occupants identified and credentials verified. Crew-served weapon positions are manned continuously. Random anti-terrorism measures are doubled in frequency. Brief all personnel at the morning huddle.

Perimeter security plan calls for two observation posts on the north berm, one on the east, and continuous roving foot patrol on the west and south sectors. Crew-served weapons emplaced in elevated bunkers with overlapping sectors of fire. Anti-vehicle ditches and serpentines at all ECPs. Indirect fire shelters within ninety seconds of any inhabited structure. Drill is conducted weekly without prior notice to validate response times.

QRF will respond to any breach of the perimeter wire or unauthorized presence inside the FOB. Standard QRF package is one squad mounted, one squad dismounted, with attached medic and EOD on call. Response time is five mikes to alert, ten mikes to launch, fifteen mikes on station for any point within one click. Daily QRF brief at zero-six-hundred.

Indirect fire alarm has sounded. All personnel take cover in the nearest hardened structure or bunker. Accountability will be conducted by chain of command within five mikes of all-clear. Counter-battery radar acquired the point of origin and has passed grid to fires. Counter-battery mission is in flight. Stand fast until further direction from the BDOC.

Standoff distance from perimeter remains a top force protection concern. Berms must be at least three meters high with anti-vehicle ditches forward. T-walls protect critical structures including the TOC, the ammo holding area, and the medical aid station. Overhead cover for sleeping quarters is required to a minimum standard. Personnel are not to congregate outdoors during designated high-threat hours.

Anti-terrorism officer has reviewed the FOB layout and identified vulnerabilities at ECP Three, where the serpentine is insufficient to defeat a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device traveling at moderate speed. Recommend installation of additional T-walls and a Jersey barrier emplacement at the speed-bump line. Mitigation must be in place within forty-eight hours. Status reports to the commander every twelve hours until complete.

Insider threat awareness training is mandatory for all personnel quarterly. Indicators include unusual interest in security procedures, attempts to access restricted areas without need-to-know, unexplained absences during high-tempo operations, and significant changes in financial or personal behavior. Report concerns to the chain of command or the unit security officer. Vigilance is a shared responsibility.

Random antiterrorism measures this week include irregular vehicle inspection patterns at ECP One, dismounted patrols varied by route and timing through the housing area, and unscheduled credential checks at the dining facility entrance. Purpose is to disrupt potential surveillance patterns and present an unpredictable security profile to any hostile observer. RAM matrix is classified at the unit level. Brief the cycle weekly at the security working group.

BDOC has alerted all stations to a Charlie alarm. Possible chemical attack imminent or in progress. MOPP level four is directed. All personnel will mask, don overgarments, boots, and gloves. Conduct buddy checks, verify seal of masks. Continue mission essential tasks in MOPP four until downgraded by the chemical officer. Decontamination station is activated at the southern wash rack. Out.

LOGPAC will roll from the BSA at zero-five-hundred. Pure-pack basis: one HEMTT cargo for Class I, one HEMTT fueler for Class III, one M977 for Class V. Route is MSR Boston to checkpoint Tango then ALT route to combat trains. Escort is one squad from the FSC with crew-served and one combat lifesaver. Arrival at combat trains rendezvous at zero-six-three-zero. Acknowledge.

Sustainment posture is amber across the formation. Class I is green, sufficient for seventy-two hours. Class III amber, fuel consumption higher than projected due to extended sector. Class V amber, expended sixty percent of basic load during last engagement, resupply requested. Class IX red on Bradley track parts, prescribed load list inadequate for current operational tempo. Brief sustainment huddle at one-eight-hundred.

Forward Support Company commander has issued a sustainment FRAGO directing emergency resupply of Class V to the lead company. Two M977 HEMTTs with palletized ammunition will move with security escort to the LRP at phase line Alpha. Trail company will provide tactical assembly area for the LOGPAC. Throughput distribution will bypass the FTCP this iteration due to time constraints.

Container Express, ConEx, holds the unit's deployable basic load of Class II and Class IV. Inventory was conducted by the supply sergeant prior to deployment, signed for by the first sergeant. Loss or damage of contents must be reported by FLIPL initiation NLT seventy-two hours after discovery. Hand receipts on file with the property book office. Audit annually or upon change of command.

Maintenance recovery operations require coordination with the BSA recovery section. Deadlined vehicle is one M1A2 with track damage from suspected IED strike. Recovery asset requested is one HET with M88 escort. Route security must be cleared prior to recovery, EOD sweep along MSR Tampa from grid juliet-three-three to checkpoint Sierra. Estimated time to ground evacuation is four hours.

Class IX repair parts shortage has created cascading deadlines across the formation. Authorized stockage list at the BSA is being expedited through the SARSS system. Critical low density items including track shoes, road wheels, and engine assemblies are on backorder from the wholesale level. Recommend the commander engage at the next sustainment huddle to push priority back to division G-4.

ROM is required for the cavalry squadron during the screen line operation. Refuel on the move site is established at the field trains command post with three HEMTT fuelers configured for simultaneous service. Throughput target is one vehicle every two minutes. Defensive posture maintained throughout, dispersed parking, no white light, terrain masking from likely enemy ground observation. Service hours are continuous from sundown to sunrise.

Mortuary affairs collection point is co-located with the medical aid station at the BSA. Procedures for handling remains are per regulation, with chain of custody documentation maintained by the mortuary affairs NCO. Personal effects are bagged and tagged separately. Coordination with the casualty assistance officer at higher headquarters is required prior to onward movement of remains to theater mortuary.

Water resupply for the dismounted patrol element will be conducted via internal load sling delivery from the aviation task force. Bird is UH-60 with sling-loaded blivet, four-zero-zero gallons potable water. LZ is the helo-pad at the patrol base, marked with VS-17 panel and infrared strobe for night delivery. Hookup team will receive sling-load operator briefing prior to bird arrival. Stand by for ETA.

Sustainment rehearsal at the BSA tonight will integrate the FSC commander, company first sergeants, the medical officer, and the maintenance warrant. Walk-through of LOGPAC routes, refuel sites, casualty evacuation chains, and prescribed load resupply will be conducted on the terrain model. Issues identified will feed the next sustainment FRAGO. Brief-back from first sergeants required.

Patrol leader gave the contact left hand-and-arm signal. Squad executed the immediate action drill, suppressing element returned fire while the maneuver element broke contact to the south. Once disengaged, the patrol consolidated at rally point Bravo. Accountability check, all PAX present. Combat ineffective casualties were zero. Patrol leader called in spot report to higher and requested permission to break contact further.

Squad encountered a hasty ambush from the wood line at fifty meters. React-to-contact drill initiated. Base of fire established by the alpha team, maneuver element from bravo team flanked right to the enemy's left. Once flanking element gained the assault line, base of fire shifted, then lifted. Assault completed, four enemy KIA confirmed. Conduct consolidation and reorganization.

Contact, contact, contact. Direction front, distance one-five-zero meters, multiple dismounts in the treeline. Squad leader directs base of fire from team Alpha, suppressing the enemy position. Team Bravo bound forward by buddy teams in five-second rushes. Reach the next covered position, then base of fire. Repeat the cycle until close enough to assault. Maintain dispersion and sectors of fire throughout the bound.

On contact, immediately return fire, take cover, locate the enemy. Suppress the enemy with accurate fires. Maneuver to a position of advantage. Assault through the objective. Consolidate and reorganize. Report up to higher with size, activity, location, unit, time, and equipment of the enemy. These are the basic battle drills every infantryman must execute reflexively under stress.

Far ambush, direction nine o'clock, two hundred meters out. Vehicle commander calls actions on contact. Gunner returns fire on identified enemy positions. Driver maneuvers vehicle to maximize armor against the threat. Dismounts remain mounted, prepared to dismount on order. Spot report transmitted to platoon net. Maneuver to a covered position and assess. Decision points: break contact, assault through, or fix and report.

Near ambush in the kill zone. Immediate action is to assault through. Volume of fire, aggressive forward movement, close with and destroy the enemy. Hesitation in the kill zone results in casualties. Once through, consolidate beyond the far side of the engagement area, accountability, reorganize, report. This drill is rehearsed in every patrol base prior to stepping off.

Sniper engagement, single shot from elevated position. Patrol drops to the deck, rolls to cover, and identifies the direction of fire by dust signature or muzzle flash. Counter-sniper drill: smoke to obscure, suppressive fire on suspected positions, displacement of exposed elements. Report to higher with assessed location of the shooter. Do not return fire unless positive identification is established.

IED detonation on lead vehicle of the convoy. Immediate actions: stop convoy outside the kill zone, establish three-sixty security, identify casualties and damaged vehicles, call up nine-line MEDEVAC if required, establish blocking positions on potential secondary device locations. EOD requested via higher. Do not move from cover until route is cleared. Press reporters and noncombatants in the area held at a distance.

Break contact drill, enemy presses the engagement from multiple directions. Squad leader designates the lead element to suppress, while the trail element bounds back to the next covered position. Rotate the role on each successive bound. Use smoke to mask movement. Continue until disengagement is achieved or contact is decisively broken. Reform at the designated rally point and account for all personnel and sensitive items.

Reaction to indirect fire. First round splash, identify direction and adjust posture. Disperse, take cover behind hardened terrain or hardened vehicles. Mark POO if possible through observation of dust, sound, or flash. Pass counter-battery grid to higher for FA mission. Account for personnel. Do not bunch up. Continue mission only after the threat is suppressed or shifted. Maintain noise and light discipline if moving.

ROE in effect for this operation are restrictive. Positive identification is required before any engagement. Hostile act or hostile intent must be observed and articulated. Self-defense remains an inherent right under any ROE. Pattern of life observations should be documented in the patrol log. Cards are carried by each team leader and reviewed at every PCC and PCI. Questions on ROE go through the chain of command.

Standing rules of engagement permit the use of necessary and proportional force in self-defense. Supplemental measures for this AOR add restrictions on collateral damage estimation, requiring two-up approval for any deliberate engagement near civilian structures or gatherings. Warning shots are not authorized. Escalation of force procedures must be exhausted prior to lethal engagement at checkpoints and observation posts.

Escalation of force procedures at the ECP follow a standard ladder. Shout to gain attention. Show weapons posture. Shove or use physical barriers if proximity allows. Shoot warning round into a backstop if authorized. Shoot to disable the vehicle. Shoot to kill if the driver is assessed as committing a hostile act. Each step must be documented in the post log.

Collateral damage estimation methodology requires identification of the weapon system, the target type, the proximity of noncombatants, and the assessed precision of the engagement. CDE level determines required approval authority for the strike. CDE Five requires combatant command approval. Lower CDE levels can be delegated to subordinate echelons. Failure to follow CDE procedures may result in a credible incident investigation.

ROE card carried by each soldier contains the abbreviated rules, the escalation of force procedures, the standing self-defense rule, and the points of contact for legal advice on the ground. The full ROE document is maintained at the company TOC. Any ROE update is briefed at the morning huddle. Soldiers must acknowledge updates by signature on the unit roster.

Hostile act is defined as an attack or other use of force against US forces or other designated persons and property. Hostile intent is the threat of imminent use of force. Both standards justify the use of proportional force in self-defense, but commanders should document the articulable indicators that led to the determination. Legal review post-engagement is standard practice.

Positive identification standard requires reasonable certainty that the proposed target is a legitimate military objective. This is a higher standard than mere suspicion. Indicators include observed weapons, hostile actions, communications intercepts properly authorized, and pattern of life consistent with combatant activity. PID is documented in the after-action report along with the engagement decision rationale.

Use of force continuum at the entry control point begins with verbal commands in the local language and English, supplemented by hand and arm signals. Visual deterrents include raised weapons, laser dazzlers, and posted signage. Physical barriers include serpentines, speed bumps, and rising bollards. Lethal force is the last resort and only when an articulable hostile act or hostile intent is observed.

Civilian casualty mitigation is a command imperative. Tactical patience is preferred over hasty engagement. Pattern of life development reduces the risk of misidentification. Battle damage assessment must include collateral damage observation. Reports of civilian casualties trigger a CIVCAS incident process, which includes immediate notification, on-scene assessment, condolence payments where appropriate, and lessons learned.

Detention authority under the current ROE permits temporary detention of individuals assessed as posing a threat to the force or as having intelligence value. Detainees must be treated humanely. Five S's apply: search, silence, segregate, safeguard, speed. Tag with date, time, place of capture, capturing unit. Process through the detainee holding area within seventy-two hours.

Patrol base occupation drill: leader's recon confirms suitability, then alpha team provides security while the rest of the platoon files into the position. Once inside, R&S teams emplace, claymores set, sectors of fire confirmed, range cards completed. Priority of work follows: security, weapons maintenance, personal hygiene, rest. No more than one-third of the element will be at less than full alert at any time.

Selection criteria for patrol base location include cover and concealment, drainage, defensibility, dispersion potential, away from known human and animal trails, away from natural lines of drift, and sufficient distance from likely enemy avenues of approach. Avoid hilltops, ridgelines, and topographic features that are obvious to the enemy. Patrol base is occupied no longer than twenty-four hours.

Recon and security teams depart the patrol base at last light to clear the immediate vicinity and emplace early warning devices. Cloverleaf patrol pattern is standard. Teams return prior to BMNT. Negative contact is the desired report. Any contact or sign indicates compromise and triggers the displacement plan. Patrol leader monitors team progress on the platoon net using prearranged sitreps.

Priority of work in the patrol base proceeds in order: weapons and equipment maintenance, personal hygiene, water and rations consumption, rest. Each task is conducted by no more than one-third of the element at a time, the remainder maintaining security. Squad leaders supervise the work cycle and ensure all critical tasks are completed before the platoon transitions to the next phase.

Triangular patrol base configuration provides three-sixty coverage with crew-served weapons or automatic weapons at each apex. Interior is reserved for the patrol leader's CP, the medic position, and the consolidation point. Listening posts are emplaced fifty to one hundred meters forward of each apex, rotating every two to four hours. Internal communication is wire if available, otherwise hand signals.

Stand-to is conducted at BMNT and EENT. The entire patrol is at full alert, weapons oriented to assigned sectors, no movement except as required to occupy fighting positions. Stand-to lasts approximately thirty minutes, allowing the patrol leader to confirm the security posture and the enemy's likely actions during these vulnerable transition periods. Resume normal cycle on the patrol leader's signal.

Departure of the patrol base requires a leader's recon of the planned route, security elements posted at the release point, and a head count and sensitive items check before stepping off. Light and noise discipline are absolute. Last action before departure is to sterilize the position: police all trash, fill in hasty fighting positions if time permits, recover all wire and pyrotechnics.

Sleep plan in the patrol base allocates four hours per soldier across a twelve-hour cycle. One-third remains on security at all times. Squad leaders rotate by sector, ensuring overlapping coverage during transitions. Patrol leader and platoon sergeant maintain awareness of the cycle and adjust based on threat level. Sleep is permitted only in designated locations within the perimeter, weapon in hand.

Emergency displacement from the patrol base is signaled by predetermined audio signal, typically two whistle blasts or radio code. All elements collapse to the nearest rally point per the patrol order. Compromise is assumed. Sensitive items are accounted for at the rally point. Movement away from the compromised position is rapid but tactical, maintaining dispersion and sectors of fire.

Resupply at the patrol base is coordinated through the platoon sergeant and conducted at night to maintain concealment. LRP is established away from the patrol base location to prevent compromise. Throughput is rapid, no congregating, no white light, sensitive items signed for. Trash and packaging is policed prior to departure from the LRP. Resupply confirmation transmitted to higher upon completion.

Convoy departure brief covered route, order of march, vehicle commander roles, action on contact, action at halts, communications, and emergency procedures. Lead vehicle has the route card and primary navigation. Trail vehicle maintains rear security and conducts head counts at each scheduled halt. Speed band is forty to fifty kilometers per hour, intervals at fifty meters in open terrain, twenty-five meters in restricted terrain.

Order of march for the convoy is lead vehicle MRAP one-one, then HEMTT two-one through two-five carrying Class V, then HMMWV three-one, ambulance four-one in the middle, command vehicle five-one with the convoy commander, and trail MRAP six-one. Intervals adjusted based on threat level and terrain. Communications via FM secure, backup is hand and arm signals at halts.

Counter-IED procedures for the convoy include EOD sweep of the route prior to departure where feasible, route reconnaissance overflight when available, varied departure times, and randomized routing within the planned scheme. Vehicle commanders scan for known IED indicators: disturbed earth, debris piles, command wires, suspicious dismounts on the route. Distance to potential threats is the primary mitigation.

Action at the short halt: vehicles stop in herringbone formation, alternating to opposite sides of the road, weapons oriented outboard. Gunners scan for threats. Drivers remain at the wheel. Dismounts dismount only on order. Halts under ten minutes. Long halts require local security with dismount teams pushing out to three-sixty coverage. Convoy commander walks the line and checks each vehicle.

Convoy commander conducts a final PCI prior to roll. Each vehicle commander reports up: communications check, fuel status, ammunition status, sensitive items count, medical bag, recovery equipment, and water. Any deadline issue is reported. Bumper numbers verified. Manifests checked against actual personnel and cargo. Departure briefing confirms the order of march, contingencies, and escalation of force procedures.

Reaction to ambush is to push through the kill zone if possible. Vehicles do not stop in the kill zone. Gunners return fire on identified threats. Damaged vehicles are pushed by trail vehicles or recovered later. Casualties are extracted at the safe area beyond the kill zone. Convoy commander reports up immediately with grid, size of attacking force, casualties, and damage. Higher provides QRF as available.

VBIED standoff requires immediate hard turn or push through, not stop. Vehicle commanders watch for high-speed approach vehicles, erratic driving, or vehicles parked along the route. Escalation of force is rapid but proceeds through the standard steps. Crew-served weapons engage at the limit of effective range if escalation is warranted. After the engagement, secure the area, summon EOD, account for personnel.

Convoy formation in restricted terrain requires closer intervals and slower speeds. Lead vehicle picks the line. Trail vehicle counts vehicles through each chokepoint. Vehicle commanders maintain communications, report up on any abnormality. Civilian traffic is held at a safe distance using local national interpreter announcements, hand signals, and vehicle posture. Movement resumes only when the route is reasonably clear.

Convoy arrival at the destination requires occupy and secure procedures. Vehicles enter the perimeter in numerical order, park in dispersed configuration, dismounts establish local security. Manifest reconciliation by the trail vehicle commander. Sensitive items verified. Casualties processed through the aid station if any. Vehicle status report to higher. Drivers conduct post-operational checks. Maintenance reported to the FSC.

Convoy AAR conducted within thirty minutes of arrival. Topics covered include route observations, threats encountered, lessons learned on actions on contact, comms performance, vehicle performance, and recommendations for the next iteration. Inputs feed the lessons learned database at the BSA. Vehicle commanders document significant events in the daily log. Convoy commander signs the trip ticket and files the after-action.

Raid is a limited objective operation with the purpose of seizing personnel, equipment, or intelligence, then withdrawing rapidly. Phases include planning, infiltration, actions on the objective, exfiltration. Planning requires detailed target package, IPB, route analysis, sustainment plan, and contingency development. Rehearsals occur at full mission profile when time permits, otherwise key tasks are walked through at minimum.

Raid element task organization typically includes assault, support, security, and reserve elements. Assault element closes with and clears the objective. Support element provides suppressive fire and isolates the objective. Security element prevents enemy reinforcement and provides early warning. Reserve element is committed at decisive moments or to handle contingencies. Each element has a primary, alternate, and contingency task.

Actions on the objective for the raid include breach, assault, clear, secure, exploit. Breach is conducted by the breach team using mechanical, explosive, ballistic, or thermal methods as appropriate. Assault element follows immediately through the breach point. Clearing rooms or trench lines uses standard close quarters battle procedures. Securing the objective involves a hasty defense oriented against the most likely enemy reaction.

Sensitive site exploitation is a critical phase of any raid against a structure or compound. SSE team is tasked to collect documents, electronics, biometric data on personnel, and any intelligence-of-value items. Photograph rooms before disturbing them. Tag and bag evidence per the chain of custody procedure. SSE time on target is windowed by the assault commander, typically under thirty minutes.

Infiltration to the objective area can be conducted by foot, vehicle, aviation insertion, or maritime insertion. Each method has advantages and constraints regarding stealth, speed, lift capacity, and weather dependency. Foot infiltration provides the lowest signature but the slowest tempo. Aviation insertion provides speed at the cost of audible and visual signature. Method is selected based on time available and OPSEC considerations.

Exfiltration plan addresses primary, alternate, contingency, and emergency routes. Time on target is windowed to limit enemy reaction. Withdrawal initiates on the assault commander's call, typically by predetermined signal or radio call. Movement is rapid but tactical, maintaining sectors of fire. Security element provides rear guard. Recovery of all personnel, equipment, and sensitive items is confirmed at the link-up rally point.

Risk assessment for the raid identifies threats to mission accomplishment and to the force. Threats are categorized by likelihood and severity, then assigned mitigations. Common mitigations include rehearsals, pre-combat checks and inspections, redundancy in critical systems, contingency planning, and on-call enabler support such as CAS, MEDEVAC, and indirect fires. Residual risk is briefed to the approving authority.

Target package for the raid is developed by the S-2 in coordination with the operations cell. Contents include intelligence summary, imagery of the objective, named graphics, pattern of life summary, link analysis of associated personnel, structures floor plans where available, and likely enemy reaction templates. Target package is briefed at the OPORD and updated as new intelligence is received prior to execution.

Rehearsals for the raid follow the crawl-walk-run methodology. Initial rehearsal is on a sand table or terrain model, walking through the scheme of maneuver at a slow pace with verbal narration. Walk-phase rehearsal is at half-speed on a similar terrain. Run-phase rehearsal is at full speed in equipment with all enablers integrated. Each rehearsal includes a debrief and refinement to the plan.

Post-raid AAR captures sustains, improves, and lessons learned. Each element leader contributes observations from their portion of the operation. Issues are categorized into doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership, personnel, facilities, and policy domains. Recommended changes feed the unit's tactics, techniques, and procedures documentation. Significant lessons are shared with adjacent units and higher headquarters.

JTAC initiating Type 2 control for CAS mission. Aircraft is two-ship Alpha-One-Zero, callsign Hawg flight. Target is enemy bunker complex, grid mike-romeo seven-four-three-eight-two-one. Friendly forces three hundred meters south, marked with VS-17 panel and infrared strobe. Threat is small arms and possible MANPADs. Cleared hot, attack heading two-seven-zero. Read back restrictions. Over.

Nine-line CAS brief follows. Line one IP Tango. Line two heading two-six-zero from IP to target. Line three distance from IP four-point-five nautical miles. Line four target elevation one-eight-two-five feet. Line five target description bunker complex. Line six target location grid as briefed. Line seven mark type IR pointer. Line eight friendlies south three hundred meters. Line nine egress heading one-two-zero. Time on target one-five-two-zero Zulu.

Type 1 control requires the JTAC to visually acquire both the attacking aircraft and the target. Type 2 control requires JTAC to visually acquire the target or to confirm target via other means but not necessarily the aircraft. Type 3 control permits multiple attacks against the same target area without individual clearance for each pass. Selection depends on weather, terrain, and risk to friendly forces.

Cleared hot, weapons hot, the lead aircraft is authorized to release ordnance. Abort criteria are: loss of positive control, loss of friendly identification, weapon malfunction, friendly forces in the impact area, or any condition that increases risk above briefed level. Abort call is 'abort abort abort' with reason if available. Egress aircraft to safe altitude and reset for follow-on attack if requested.

Marking the target for CAS aircraft is conducted by JTAC with an infrared pointer, laser designator, or smoke. IR pointer is night-only and requires the pilot to be on goggles. Laser designation requires laser code synchronization between JTAC and aircraft. Smoke is day-only and is observed by visual identification. Mark precedes the cleared hot call so the pilot has time to acquire.

Danger close engagements require approval from the ground force commander, not the JTAC alone. Risk estimate distance is calculated based on weapon system, target type, terrain, and friendly posture. Approval is required when friendly forces are within RED distance of the planned point of impact. Approving authority documents the decision in the post-mission report. Risk is briefed prior to weapons release.

Battle damage assessment from the CAS strike is reported to the supported ground force commander as soon as possible after the engagement. Format includes number of targets engaged, ordnance expended, type and number of munitions, observed effects, estimated casualties, and confirmation of friendly status. BDA feeds the targeting cycle and may trigger restrike requests if effects are insufficient.

Check-in with CAS aircraft includes aircraft callsign, number of aircraft, type of aircraft, position, altitude, ordnance loadout, station time remaining, and any abort codes. JTAC acknowledges and provides the situation update including weather, threats, target priority, and ground force scheme of maneuver. Following check-in, JTAC walks the pilot's eyes onto the target area through visual references.

Pilot reports 'in' as the attack run is initiated, 'wings level' as the weapon is released, and 'off' as the aircraft egresses the target area. JTAC observes the weapon effect and provides battle damage assessment to the pilot. Follow-on attack is requested if needed. Time on target overall is closely managed to minimize aircraft exposure to threat systems on the ground.

Final attack heading restrictions are determined by the ground force commander to ensure aircraft do not fly over friendly positions or known threat envelopes. JTAC briefs the FAH to the aircraft as part of the nine-line. Deviation from the FAH requires re-clearance. Departure restrictions, such as no overfly of populated areas, are similarly briefed and enforced. Aircraft compliance is observed and documented.

Intelligence preparation of the battlefield is a four-step continuous process. Step one defines the operational environment, including terrain, weather, and civil considerations. Step two describes environmental effects on operations. Step three evaluates the threat by identifying enemy capabilities, doctrine, and order of battle. Step four determines threat courses of action, producing the most likely and most dangerous COA templates for the commander's decision.

MCOO development integrates terrain factors observation and fields of fire, avenues of approach, key terrain, obstacles, and cover and concealment. Each factor is overlaid on the operational graphic to produce a composite picture of how the terrain shapes friendly and enemy options. MCOO drives the IPB process and directly informs the commander's scheme of maneuver and the placement of obstacles and weapon systems.

Named areas of interest are geographic locations where collection assets are tasked to confirm or deny aspects of the enemy's most likely course of action. Each NAI is tied to a specific PIR and an indicator. Collection plan assigns assets to NAIs based on suitability, availability, and risk. Updates from collection feed the staff's continuous reassessment of enemy intent and disposition.

Priority intelligence requirements drive the entire collection effort. PIRs are commander-approved and reflect the information the commander needs to make a decision. Typical PIRs include enemy main effort location, timing of enemy attack, location of enemy reserve, and enemy logistical sustainability. Each PIR is decomposed into indicators which are then assigned to NAIs and collection assets.

Pattern of life analysis observes routine activity in the AO over time to detect anomalies that indicate enemy activity. Indicators include changes in vehicle traffic, market activity, population movement, electronic emissions, and religious or political gatherings. POL baselines are built through sustained collection. Departures from baseline trigger further investigation and may shape kinetic or non-kinetic operations.

Enemy course of action analysis produces the most likely and most dangerous COA, with sketches and narratives. Most likely COA represents the enemy's preferred approach based on doctrine, capability, and observed indicators. Most dangerous COA is what the enemy could do that would cause the greatest harm if executed. Both COAs are wargamed against friendly options to identify decision points and branches.

Threat templates depict enemy doctrinal disposition under specific conditions. A doctrinal motorized rifle company in the offense, for example, attacks with two platoons forward and one in depth, on a frontage of roughly fifteen hundred meters, supported by an artillery battalion. Threat templates are then refined into situation templates by integrating terrain and weather constraints to produce the most likely enemy disposition.

Event template synthesizes the threat COA, the terrain analysis, and the friendly scheme of maneuver into a single product that depicts where and when key enemy actions are expected to occur. Decision points for the commander are tied to specific events on the template. The collection plan is keyed to the event template, ensuring assets are positioned to observe critical indicators in time to inform decisions.

Civil considerations in IPB are captured under the ASCOPE framework: areas, structures, capabilities, organizations, people, and events. Each category is evaluated for its impact on operations. ASCOPE analysis informs not only kinetic planning but also stability and civil-military operations. Civilian leaders, religious sites, infrastructure dependencies, and significant cultural events all factor into the commander's appreciation of the operating environment.

Weather effects on operations are analyzed under five factors: visibility, winds, precipitation, cloud cover, and temperature and humidity. Each factor is evaluated for impact on personnel, equipment, and operations. Visibility affects observation and engagement ranges. Winds affect aviation, indirect fire, and smoke employment. Precipitation affects mobility, soldier endurance, and weapon function. The S-2 weather annex distills these into operational impacts.

EOD team responding to suspected IED at grid mike-romeo eight-eight-four-three-two-one. Initial assessment from the patrol element is a buried command-wire device, partially exposed. EOD team has set up the standoff at three hundred meters and is conducting a robot-mounted reconnaissance. Render safe procedures to follow once the device is positively characterized. Cordon is in place. EOD will brief the supported unit on the disposition of the device.

Five Cs of IED response: confirm, clear, cordon, check, and control. Confirm the device by visual identification without approaching. Clear personnel from the area to safe standoff. Cordon the area to prevent unauthorized entry. Check for secondary devices, command wires, and triggermen. Control the scene by establishing communications and waiting for EOD response. These procedures are drilled in every pre-deployment training cycle.

Render safe procedure for the device follows the principle of remote operation where possible. EOD team employs remotely operated tools and disruption charges to neutralize the device without close approach. If remote operation is not possible, the team conducts a hands-on render-safe in full bomb suit with maximum standoff support from the cordon. Post-blast analysis collects components for forensic exploitation.

Post-blast investigation procedures: secure the scene, photograph the crater and surrounding area in a methodical pattern, sketch the scene with measurements, collect fragments and components, document witnesses and observations, and transport collected material to the technical exploitation lab. Chain of custody is maintained throughout. Reporting follows the WIT format, which integrates with theater-wide IED defeat analysis.

Counter-IED defeat the device line of operations focuses on detecting and neutralizing the device before it functions. Detection is enabled by route clearance teams, electronic countermeasures, and pattern analysis. Neutralization is conducted by EOD teams using remote tools and disruption charges. Other lines of operation include attacking the network and training the force, all integrated into the overall counter-IED strategy.

Cleared route status is maintained by route clearance teams operating purpose-built equipment such as Husky vehicle-mounted detectors and Buffalo interrogation arms. Routes are categorized as black, red, amber, green based on threat level and recency of clearance. Status is briefed at the operations huddle and pushed to maneuver units via overlay. Recleared NLT every forty-eight hours on amber routes, daily on red.

EOD callout procedures begin with a nine-line UXO report from the discovering element. Lines include date-time of discovery, reporting activity, location, contact info, device type, resources threatened, impact on mission, NBC contamination indicators, and recommended priority for response. EOD team assesses priority based on operational impact and proximity to friendly forces or civilians. Response is scheduled accordingly.

Bomb suit operations require extensive training and physical conditioning. The suit weighs over thirty kilograms and significantly degrades mobility, dexterity, and field of view. EOD technicians work in pairs with a controller in the safe area monitoring vitals and communications. Operations in the suit are kept brief, typically under thirty minutes per session. Cooling vests and hydration are essential particularly in hot environments.

UXO disposal pit construction follows specifications to contain blast and fragmentation. Depth, diameter, and standoff from structures are dictated by the net explosive weight of the largest item to be disposed. Berms surround the pit to redirect blast upward. Demolition charges are placed in accordance with EOD methodology and standoff procedures. Post-detonation inspection confirms complete consumption of the ordnance.

Suspected radiological dispersal device requires additional protocols beyond standard EOD response. CBRN team supports the EOD response, with radiation detection equipment, contamination control measures, and downwind hazard analysis. Cordon distance is significantly expanded. Medical surveillance is briefed for all responders. Decontamination procedures are pre-positioned. Notification through CBRN channels is immediate, regardless of the time of day.

MOPP level four is the highest mission-oriented protective posture, requiring suit, mask, gloves, and overboots. Personnel in MOPP four experience significant physical degradation, including reduced visibility, heat stress, communications difficulty, and impaired fine motor function. Work-rest cycles are managed by the chain of command, with frequent rotation, hydration, and cooling. Mission-essential tasks are prioritized, non-essential activities deferred until downgrade.

Chemical agent alarm has activated at the southern perimeter. ADAM detector reading is positive for nerve agent. CBRN officer is dispatched to confirm with M8 paper. All personnel within the threat zone go to MOPP four immediately. Decontamination station is brought online. Downwind hazard area calculation is in progress. Casualty assessment ready. Atropine and pralidoxime auto-injectors are checked and accessible.

NBC1 report format includes: line alpha unit reporting, line bravo location of incident, line charlie time of incident, line delta type of attack and agent, line echo means of delivery, line foxtrot location of impact, line golf casualties, line hotel meteorological conditions, line india damage to equipment. Report is transmitted up the chain via secure means to enable theater-wide situational awareness.

Decontamination operations follow a deliberate sequence: immediate, operational, thorough, and clearance. Immediate decon is conducted within minutes of contamination using the M295 individual kit. Operational decon focuses on critical equipment and personnel within hours. Thorough decon is conducted at a brigade-level site to restore full capability. Clearance decon verifies contamination is reduced to negligible levels. Each phase requires trained personnel and specialized equipment.

Mask confidence training builds soldier trust in the protective mask. Personnel enter a chamber and experience controlled exposure to CS, validating that a properly sealed mask provides full protection. Mask fit checks are conducted at the start of each duty day in a contaminated environment. Replacement filters are inventoried at the squad level. Crews wear masks at the level briefed by the commander.

CBRN reconnaissance mission requires specialized equipment and trained operators. Fox NBCRS vehicles or comparable platforms conduct mounted reconnaissance of suspected contaminated areas. Dismounted survey teams with M256 kits validate readings. Marker sets identify confirmed contamination boundaries. Findings are reported via NBC4 message to the CBRN cell at brigade. Avoidance routes are then disseminated to maneuver elements via overlay.

Biological surveillance includes both fixed-site and mobile detection systems. Joint Biological Point Detection System provides automated detection of selected agents. Joint Biological Standoff Detection System provides standoff alert. Confirmatory analysis is conducted at theater-level laboratory. Protective measures include immunization where available, prophylaxis for known threats, and field hygiene measures. Suspected casualties are isolated and reported through medical channels.

Radiological survey teams conduct dose-rate measurements at predetermined locations within and around the suspected contaminated area. Readings are plotted on the overlay and used to calculate isodose lines. Total dose calculations are made for personnel based on time in contaminated areas. Operational exposure guidance is briefed to commanders to support risk decisions. Dosimeters are issued and read daily during operations in contaminated environments.

Atropine auto-injector training is mandatory for all personnel deployed where chemical threats are credible. In suspected nerve agent exposure, self or buddy administration of two injectors into the thigh muscle, with additional doses based on symptom severity. Pralidoxime injection is paired with atropine to reverse cholinesterase inhibition. CANA injection for seizure management. Casualties are evacuated to a higher level of care immediately after intervention.

Downwind hazard prediction is a critical CBRN staff function. Atmospheric conditions including wind speed, wind direction, stability, and inversion layer presence determine the agent's likely path and concentration. Hazard prediction models produce templates showing immediate, hazard, and casualty zones. Templates are pushed to the operations cell for incorporation into maneuver decisions. Updates are continuous as meteorological conditions change.

Weapons control status is currently weapons hold, meaning aircraft and direct fire weapons engage only in self-defense or on order. Conditions for transition to weapons tight or weapons free will be briefed at the appropriate level. Crews remain at REDCON-2 with weapons cleared, loaded, and on safe. Acquisition continues against assigned sectors. Engagement criteria are reviewed at every shift change. Vigilance is maintained throughout.

Engagement criteria for the defense include positive identification of the target as enemy combatant, target within established sector of fire, weapon system within effective range, no friendly forces in the line of fire, and no excessive risk of collateral damage. Fire commands incorporate alert, target description, range, and method of engagement. Crews execute the fire command on the gunner's call of 'identified'.

Range card for the crew-served weapon shows primary direction of fire, primary sector of fire, dead space within sector, principal direction of fire, final protective line, and TRPs. Distances and azimuths to TRPs are marked. Sector limits are physically marked with aiming stakes. Range card is filed in the position and one copy retained by the squad leader. Card is updated when weapon position is altered.

Final protective fires are pre-planned, pre-registered indirect and direct fires laid down in front of the defensive position to break up an enemy assault during a critical period. FPF is called only at decisive moments. Direct fire FPL coordinates the linear shooting of crew-served weapons across the engagement area. Crews engage continuously and at maximum rate until the assault is broken or higher orders cease fires.

Volley fire command is used to mass effects against a point target at known range. Crew responds by simultaneously aiming, calling 'identified' when on target, and firing on the leader's command 'fire'. Volley achieves first-round hit probability higher than uncoordinated fire. Volley discipline is rehearsed in dry-fire and live-fire training. Standard application is against bunkers, vehicles, or massed dismounted enemy.

Sustained rate of fire for the M240 medium machine gun is one hundred rounds per minute, in six-to-nine round bursts. Rapid rate is two hundred rounds per minute. Cyclic rate is six hundred fifty to nine hundred fifty rounds per minute and is reserved for the most critical defensive situations. Barrel changes are conducted at the specified intervals to prevent damage. Crews rehearse barrel changes under time constraints.

Battle sight zero for the rifle is established at a known distance, typically twenty-five meters. The sight is adjusted so the round impact is centered at the aim point or to the doctrinal offset. Once established, the rifle's BZO allows the soldier to engage targets at variable ranges by adjusting hold. BZO confirmation is conducted at every range opportunity and after any maintenance affecting the sight.

Crew-served weapon emplacement requires proper site selection: defilade where possible to protect the crew, primary and alternate positions, supplemental positions to cover unexpected enemy avenues, dead space identification within sector, and primary and grazing fires planning. Overhead cover and fighting position improvement are critical. Crews dig in to the standard prescribed in the unit SOP, with revetment, drainage, and field of fire clearance.

Direct fire planning at the company level integrates each weapon system into a coherent engagement plan. Sectors of fire are assigned to each crew-served weapon. Engagement areas are developed to canalize and destroy enemy formations. Trigger lines and TRPs are designated to initiate massed fires at decisive moments. The fire plan is rehearsed and tested with dry runs prior to enemy contact. Adjustments are made based on rehearsal findings.

Fire command sequence per doctrine: alert, target, weapons or ammunition, direction, range, method of engagement, control. Example: 'Squad, frontal, machine gun, twelve o'clock, two hundred meters, fire at my command, ready, fire'. The sequence is brief, complete, and unambiguous. Each element conveys necessary information to crews. Adjustments and corrections follow the same format. Repetition for clarity is permitted but conciseness is preferred under stress.

Measures of performance assess whether a task was completed correctly and on time. MOPs answer 'are we doing things right'. Example MOPs for a deliberate attack include time from line of departure to objective, percentage of friendly losses, number of enemy positions cleared. MOPs are quantitative and observable. Each MOP is tied to a task and standard. Failure to meet a MOP triggers review of the execution.

Measures of effectiveness assess whether the actions are producing the desired outcomes. MOEs answer 'are we doing the right things'. Example MOEs for a stability operation include reduction in attacks per week, increase in local security force capability, increase in civilian confidence in the government. MOEs require longer observation windows and may be qualitative. Trend analysis is more important than single data points.

Assessment framework for the operation links tasks to MOPs, lines of effort to MOEs, and end state to the operational and strategic objectives. Each MOP and MOE has indicators that are collected through the running estimate. Trends are tracked over time and presented to the commander at the weekly assessment update. Adjustments to lines of effort are recommended based on observed trends and the commander's intent.

MOE selection requires careful consideration of what indicators truly reflect the outcome being measured. Lazy MOEs measure activity, not effectiveness. A weak MOE for combatting an insurgent network is the number of detentions; a stronger MOE is the reduction in attacks attributed to that network over time. Staff officers should challenge proposed MOEs for relevance, observability, and freedom from manipulation by friendly activity.

Running estimate maintained by each staff section integrates MOPs and MOEs into a continuously updated picture of operations. The G-3 running estimate tracks force disposition and operational tempo. The G-2 running estimate tracks enemy situation and trends. The G-4 running estimate tracks sustainment posture. Each estimate feeds the commander's daily and weekly assessment battle rhythm.

Commander's critical information requirements are decomposed into PIRs for the enemy and FFIRs for friendly forces. CCIRs drive the collection and reporting plan. PIRs and FFIRs are reviewed at the daily commander's update brief and adjusted based on the operational situation. Each CCIR is owned by a staff section and has assigned indicators, NAIs, and collection assets. CCIRs not being answered are flagged for action.

Decision support template integrates the staff's assessment of friendly and enemy actions into a graphical product that highlights decision points for the commander. Each decision point has an associated trigger, the required information, and the decision options available. The DST is updated continuously and reviewed at the commander's update brief. It is the operational nerve center for commander's decision making during execution.

Assessment working group meets weekly to review MOPs, MOEs, and trends. Participants include the chief of staff, key staff officers, and the senior intelligence officer. Findings are presented to the commander at the next operations and intelligence brief. Recommendations for refining lines of effort, reallocating resources, or adjusting the campaign plan emerge from the working group. Documentation of decisions and rationale is maintained for transparency.

End state criteria specify the conditions that must exist for the operation to be considered complete. Military end state typically includes the destruction or degradation of enemy military capability to a specified level, the establishment of friendly control over key terrain, and the transition of responsibility to follow-on forces or partner authorities. End state is the ultimate yardstick against which all MOEs are oriented.

Performance versus effectiveness distinction is critical to honest assessment. A unit can be performing every task to standard while still failing to achieve the desired effect. This often indicates a faulty operational concept rather than a lack of effort. The assessment process must surface such disconnects and feed them back into planning. Commanders who reward performance without examining effectiveness can find themselves successfully executing the wrong strategy.

Command and control is exercised through a TOC manned around the clock by the battle captain, battle NCO, fires officer, and intelligence watch.
